parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is represented by an electric field line.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Two point charges *P* and *Q* are placed 0.120 m apart as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text:
The charge of *P* is +4.0 nC and the charge of *Q* is −7.2 nC.

Determine the distance from *P* of the point on the line joining the two charges where the electric potential is zero.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain, without calculation, whether the electric field strength is zero at the same point at which the electric potential is zero.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
An electron is positioned at point *X*, equidistant from both *P* and *Q*, as shown in Fig. 4.2.

[[fig:f2]]

On Fig. 4.2, draw an arrow to represent the direction of the resultant force acting on the electron.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: Two charges, P and Q, are shown 0.120 m apart, with P marked +4.0 nC and Q marked −7.2 nC.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: Points P and Q are shown on either side of point X, with X equidistant from both.
